name: Madagascar: the RN7, the baobabs and an island

cities.base: Isoraka or the Haute-Ville around Ambatonakanga. Both put the restaurants, the stairs and the Rova within walking distance, which matters because Tana traffic can turn four kilometres into an hour. Iv
cities.name: Antananarivo

cities.base: Andasibe village itself, or the lodges on the Mantadia road five to ten minutes north. The indri call between 07:00 and 09:00, so anything more than fifteen minutes from the gate costs you the whole p
cities.name: Andasibe (Analamazaotra)

cities.base: The strip between Ranomafana village and the Ambodiamontana park entrance, which is about 6 km of road with most of the lodges on it. Sleeping in Fianarantsoa instead adds three hours to a 07:00 start
cities.name: Ranomafana

cities.base: Ranohira or the lodges strung along the RN7 within fifteen minutes of it. The good ones sit out on the escarpment facing the massif, which is what you are paying for. Ranohira to the northern canyons
cities.name: Isalo (Ranohira)

cities.base: The Nosy Kely spit, where the hotels, the beach and the restaurants are, about forty minutes from the baobabs. Getting here sanely means the Madagascar Airlines domestic flight from Tana, roughly an h
cities.name: Morondava

cities.base: The west coast between Madirokely and Belle Vue for boats and food, or Andilana at the north end for the sand and quiet. Avoid basing in Ambatoloaka itself. Reached by air from Tana in about eighty mi
cities.name: Nosy Be

places.name: Rova of Antananarivo (Manjakamiadana)
places.note: The queen's palace burned in 1995 and the long reconstruction finished at the end of 2025, so what you walk through is new stone around an old silhouette. The view over the whole city is the better half of the ticket; confirm hours and price at the gate because both have moved repeatedly.

places.name: Andafiavaratra Palace Museum
places.note: The pink palace of prime minister Rainilaiarivony, holding the objects firefighters pulled out of the Rova fire, including Ranavalona's crown. Labelling is thin and the lighting is worse, so go with a guide or you will see furniture.

places.name: The Haute-Ville stairs, Ambondrona to Andohalo
places.note: Tana only makes sense on foot, climbing the stone staircases between the lower town and the ridge past brick houses and Andohalo cathedral. Steep, uneven and not to be done after dark.

places.name: Analakely market and the Escalier
places.note: The old Zoma was broken up decades ago, so this is the surviving daily sprawl of stalls under the escalier and along Avenue de l'Independance. Go early with your driver or guide and carry nothing in an outside pocket.

places.name: Parc Botanique et Zoologique de Tsimbazaza
places.note: A tired zoo with a serious paleontology hall: elephant bird eggs, subfossil lemur skeletons and an aye-aye you are unlikely to see wild. Enclosures are small and some visitors find it upsetting.

places.name: Lemurs' Park
places.note: A private reserve on the Katsaoka river with nine species of rescued lemur free-ranging in restored bush, about an hour out on the RN1. It is a good first afternoon while you are jet-lagged and a waste of a morning once you have been to Andasibe.

places.name: Croc Farm Ivato
places.note: A crocodile farm and small zoo ten minutes from the airport with a restaurant that serves crocodile. Its only real use is burning a long connection or a late departure day.

places.name: La Varangue
places.note: French Malagasy cooking in a colonial villa crammed with the owner's collection of enamel signs and automata. It is the dependable good dinner in Tana rather than the exciting one, and you should book.

places.name: Hotel Sakamanga bar and dining room
places.note: The crossroads bar of Malagasy travel, where zebu steak, cold THB and every driver, pilot and guide in the country eventually turn up. Loud, cheap and useful for information.

places.name: Chez Mariette
places.note: Madagascar's best known home cook, who takes one table a day and feeds it what she has decided to cook, romazava and ravitoto included. Book at least a day ahead and confirm she is still receiving, because the kitchen has slowed in recent years.

places.name: Marche Artisanal de la Digue
places.note: Raffia, zebu horn, Antaimoro paper and embroidered cloth in a long line of sheds on the airport road. Opening prices are roughly triple, and the rosewood carvings are illegal to take home.

places.name: Analamazaotra Reserve, the indri circuit
places.note: The indri call between about 07:00 and 09:00 and that song, carrying a kilometre through wet forest, is the reason the whole eastern leg exists. A guide is compulsory and allocated at the gate, the short circuit is flat and crowded, and the longer one loses most of the group.

places.name: Mantadia National Park
places.note: An hour of broken track each way in a 4x4 for diademed sifaka, black-and-white ruffed lemur and genuinely tall primary rainforest. Wetter, steeper and almost empty compared with Analamazaotra, and the transport has to be arranged the day before.

places.name: VOIMMA Reserve night walk
places.note: Night walking inside the national park is banned, so every night walk here happens on community land along the road, and VOIMMA's is the village-run one. An hour of torchlight finds mouse lemurs, leaf-tailed geckos and several chameleons.

places.name: Association Mitsinjo forest station
places.note: Community-restored forest with its own habituated indri group and an amphibian breeding lab for the golden mantella. Quieter than the national park, cheaper, and the money stays in Andasibe.

places.name: Torotorofotsy marsh
places.note: A Ramsar wetland where guides look for golden mantella frogs, greater bamboo lemur and marsh birds. Muddy to the knee and only worth a morning if you already have the indri in the bag.

places.name: Lemur Island at Vakona Forest Lodge
places.note: Hand-fed lemurs on an island they cannot swim off, which will sit on your head for a banana. It photographs beautifully and it is not wildlife, so do it after the park or not at all.

places.name: Vakona Forest Lodge dining room
places.note: The one proper dining room in the Andasibe area, with a fire lit most evenings because 900 metres of rainforest gets cold. Service slows to a crawl when two group buses arrive together.

places.name: Feon'ny Ala
places.note: The long-standing budget bungalows by the river, where the indri are audible from the terrace at dawn. Food is simple and the dining room fills with groups at 19:00 sharp.

places.name: Mantadia Lodge terrace
places.note: Stone terrace looking down the valley with a Dzama rum in hand, which is about the whole of an Andasibe evening. Check with reception first if you are not staying.

places.name: Peyrieras Reptile Reserve, Marozevo
places.note: A private chameleon and gecko farm on the RN2 roughly halfway back to Tana, where the animals are placed on branches for your camera. It is a photo studio rather than a reserve, useful only if the wild ones have eluded you.

places.name: Andasibe station and the Moramanga road
places.note: The colonial-era station on the Tana to Tamatave line, now used by occasional freight and a lot of laundry. Ten minutes of interest on the walk to dinner and no more.

places.name: Talatakely circuit, Ranomafana
places.note: Stairs and switchbacks through dripping montane forest where the spotters usually deliver golden bamboo lemur and Milne-Edwards's sifaka before 10:00. A guide is compulsory, spotters are extra and expected, and leeches are normal after rain.

places.name: Vohiparara circuit
places.note: Higher, colder and far less trodden than Talatakely, with the better odds on greater bamboo lemur and the endemic ground-rollers. Steep, slick clay underfoot and no shelter if the mist comes down.
places.neighborhood: Vohiparara, RN25 west of the park gate

places.name: The RN25 night walk
places.note: Everybody walks the same 800 metres of verge with head torches, because night access inside the park is not allowed. It is crowded and slightly absurd, and you still see mouse lemurs, chameleons and a giraffe-necked weevil.

places.name: Centre ValBio
places.note: Patricia Wright's research station above the park, which sometimes shows visitors the labs and the current fieldwork. Ask your guide to call ahead, because whether it happens depends entirely on who is in residence.

places.name: Ranomafana thermal baths
places.note: The hot spring the town is named for, delivered into a concrete pool that has seen better decades. Cheap, genuinely hot, and full of Malagasy families at the weekend.

places.name: Setam Lodge restaurant
places.note: The reliable dinner in Ranomafana, with a fire going and the valley below the windows. Getting to it means a lot of steps in the dark.

places.name: Hotel Centrest Sejour
places.note: Swiss-run, wood-panelled and quietly the best value plate on this stretch of the RN25. Order the plat du jour and do not expect speed.

places.name: Anja Community Reserve
places.note: Around three hundred ring-tailed lemurs living among granite boulders on thirty hectares that the village itself runs and profits from. It is done as a stop on the drive south, not as a day trip, and the light and the lemurs are both better before 09:00.
places.neighborhood: Anja, 13 km south of Ambalavao on the RN7

places.name: Fabrique de Papier Antemoro, Ambalavao
places.note: Mulberry bark pounded, pressed and dried with flowers laid into it, demonstrated in about ten minutes before you are steered to the shop. A fair enough leg-stretch on a very long driving day.

places.name: Ambalavao zebu market
places.note: The largest cattle market in Madagascar, with herds walked up from the deep south over weeks by drovers who sleep with them. It runs Wednesday and Thursday, it is dusty and loud, and nothing about it is arranged for you.

places.name: Fianarantsoa Haute-Ville
places.note: The old upper town of nineteenth-century brick houses and churches on a hill, half restored and half falling in. Take a local guide, because the lanes are a maze and the descent is steep.

places.name: The Piscine Naturelle
places.note: Two hours over bare sandstone and up a shallow canyon to a cold green pool under pandanus, then the same ground back with no shade at all. Start at 06:30 or you will do the return in the worst heat of the day.

places.name: Namaza and the Cascade des Nymphes
places.note: A shaded canyon walk to a waterfall, with ring-tailed lemurs and Verreaux's sifaka coming down to the Namaza campsite in the afternoon. The plateau crossing to reach it is exposed and hot.

places.name: Canyon des Makis and Canyon des Rats
places.note: An hour of sand track and then two narrow canyons that hold water and lemurs deep into the dry season. If you only get one full day in Isalo, this is the one to spend it on.
places.neighborhood: Northern Isalo, about 25 km from Ranohira

places.name: La Fenetre de l'Isalo
places.note: A hole in a rock that frames the sunset, plus forty vehicles, a row of souvenir stalls and everyone's tripod. It costs nothing and ten minutes of it is plenty.

places.name: The Bara tombs in the cliffs
places.note: Bara burial niches wedged high in the sandstone, which every guide points out from the road into the park. You look from below; approaching them is fady and you will be told so.

places.name: Isalo Interpretation Centre
places.note: The small MNP display on the massif's geology, its endemic plants and Bara custom, in the building where you settle fees and meet your guide anyway. Twenty minutes of content, and worth doing before you walk rather than after.

places.name: Isalo Rock Lodge terrace
places.note: Stone terraces facing the massif, which turns orange then purple for about twenty minutes after the sun goes. Non-residents are usually welcome for a drink, but ring in July and August.

places.name: Le Relais de la Reine
places.note: Built into the rock with a French kitchen, a stable of horses and the most comfortable dinner between Fianarantsoa and Tulear. Book ahead in the July to August season.

places.name: Le Jardin du Roy
places.note: Same owners, a stone dining room and a garden planted with the region's succulents and pachypodiums. It is where the RN7 groups eat, so 19:30 can be a scrum.
places.neighborhood: Beside Le Relais de la Reine

places.name: Ranohira market
places.note: Fruit, dried fish, plastic buckets and phone credit, serving a town that is otherwise entirely hotels and park offices. Fifteen minutes, and the only unstaged thing in Ranohira.

places.name: Ilakaka sapphire town
places.note: A sapphire rush town of tarpaulin, pits and foreign buyers that grew from nothing after 1998 and has the social problems to match. Look from the car, keep the camera down, and do not buy stones.

places.name: Allee des Baobabs at sunset
places.note: Twenty-odd Grandidier's baobabs standing over a dirt road, and the last forty minutes of light is the entire reason to be in western Madagascar. A small parking fee applies and the sunset crowd is substantial.

places.name: Allee des Baobabs at sunrise
places.note: The same trees with a tenth of the people and zebu carts using the road as a road rather than a set. Leave Morondava by 04:45 to be in place.

places.name: Baobab Amoureux
places.note: Two Adansonia za trunks wound round each other, with a love story attached and a boy who will tell it for a small tip. Fifteen extra minutes, and only because you are already up there.
places.neighborhood: Beyond the Allee, off the RN8

places.name: Kirindy Forest day walk
places.note: Dry deciduous forest run by CNFEREF where Verreaux's sifaka and red-fronted brown lemur are close to guaranteed and the fossa is a matter of luck. Two hours of rough road each way, and the forest is largely shut to visitors in the rains.

places.name: Kirindy night walk
places.note: Madame Berthe's mouse lemur, the smallest primate alive, plus giant jumping rats and pale fork-marked lemurs in the torch beam. It means sleeping in the basic Kirindy bungalows, because driving that track back at night is a bad idea.

places.name: Nosy Kely beach spit
places.note: A sand spit of hotels and pirogues that the Mozambique Channel is eating at several metres a year, with the ruins to prove it. Swimmable and not beautiful, and fine for one evening.

places.name: Chez Maggie
places.note: The long-running beach hotel and kitchen, grilled fish and cold beer at a table on the sand. Confirm it is open before you build a day round it, because Morondava closes down hard in low season.

places.name: Marche de Morondava
places.note: Crabs, dried shark, tamarind, enamelware and no tourist layer whatsoever. Half an hour, early, and take your guide.

places.name: Sunset drink on the Nosy Kely front
places.note: The hotel terraces on the spit face straight west over the channel, which is the consolation on a night you are not out at the baobabs. Beer is cheap and the mosquitoes arrive with the dark.

places.name: Belo sur Tsiribihina and the river barge
places.note: The Tsiribihina crossing on a flat barge, which takes an hour or most of a day depending on tide, queue and whether the ramp has washed out. Only do this if you are continuing north to the Tsingy.

places.name: Tsingy de Bemaraha
places.note: Limestone blades, via ferrata and one of the strangest landscapes on earth, reached by two hard days of track each way from Morondava and closed outright in the rains. It needs four to five days on its own and it does not fit a fourteen day trip that also drives the RN7.

places.name: Lokobe Reserve by pirogue
places.note: Paddled out from Ambatozavavy in a dugout and then walked slowly through the last real forest on the island for black lemurs, panther chameleons and sleeping boa. The paddle is about forty-five minutes each way with no shade, so take a hat and mean it.

places.name: Nosy Tanikely marine reserve
places.note: The most reliable snorkelling you can reach from Nosy Be, with turtles on the shallow reef and a lighthouse walk for the view over the channel. It is a paying marine park and every boat lands within the same hour, so go on the earliest departure.

places.name: Nosy Komba, Ampangorina village
places.note: Black lemurs that have been fed bananas for forty years and a lane of embroidery stalls behind them. The village is real and worth the walk uphill; the lemur encounter is staged and everyone knows it.

places.name: Mont Passot at sunset
places.note: The high point over the crater lakes, which are sacred, full of crocodile in local account and absolutely not for swimming. There is a small fee at the barrier and the whole island drives up for the sunset.

places.name: Andilana beach
places.note: The best sand on Nosy Be, wide, pale and shelving gently, with beach kitchens at the north end. Sunday it fills with families up from Hell-Ville, which is the version worth seeing.

places.name: Nosy Sakatia turtle snorkel
places.note: Green turtles grazing seagrass in water shallow enough to stand in, ten minutes by boat from Chanty Beach. Calmer, cheaper and far less booked than Tanikely.
places.neighborhood: Nosy Sakatia, off the west coast

places.name: Whale shark snorkelling
places.note: September to early December, spotted from the boat and entered quietly a few at a time under an agreed code of conduct. Numbers swing hard year to year and no honest operator will promise you an animal.

places.name: Hell-Ville (Andoany) old town and market
places.note: Colonial arcades, a working port and a market that is busiest at the end of the week. It is the only part of Nosy Be with a past rather than a brochure.

places.name: Ylang-ylang distillery
places.note: The island's other economy, distilled in copper stills that look a hundred years old, and the smell reaches the road. Fifteen minutes of real interest followed by the essential oil counter.

places.name: Ambatoloaka strip
places.note: The tourist strip: bars, touts, loud music and an open sex trade involving very young women that you cannot look past. Know what you are booking before you take a hotel here.

places.name: Nosy Iranja
places.note: Two islands joined by a sandbar that appears at low tide, about two hours each way in an open boat. It is a long rough day for a photograph, and any swell cancels it outright.

outings.why: Gate at 06:30, guide allocated on the spot and compulsory, then two to three hours of flat wet trail listening for the indri and walking to whichever family the spotters have found. The forest is warm and the ground is greasy; the difficult
outings.name: The Analamazaotra indri circuit
outings.season: All year. September to November and April to May are the bes
outings.fallback: The Mitsinjo station opposite, which has its own indri group and a quarter of the people.

outings.why: An hour of rutted track each way in a hired 4x4, then a steep day in primary rainforest for diademed sifaka and black-and-white ruffed lemur. Arrange the vehicle the day before; there is nothing to hire at the gate.
outings.name: Mantadia, the diademed sifaka circuit
outings.season: All year, but the track is unreliable January to March.
outings.fallback: Torotorofotsy marsh, half the day and half the mud.

outings.why: Night access inside the national park is banned, so this happens on community forest by the road from about 18:00. One hour of torchlight for mouse lemurs, chameleons and leaf-tailed geckos, done standing on a verge with other groups.
outings.name: The VOIMMA night walk
outings.fallback: The Mitsinjo night walk on the other side of the road.

outings.why: Around 410 km of tarmac that is mostly sound and occasionally not, through Ambatolampy, Antsirabe and the Betsileo rice terraces. Trucks, zebu carts and villages hold the average to about 40 km per hour, which is why nearly everyone sleeps
outings.name: Tana to Ranomafana on the RN7
outings.season: All year. Landslips on the Ranomafana descent are a January
outings.fallback: Break at Antsirabe and arrive the next morning.

outings.why: Stairs, roots and switchbacks in montane forest, with a compulsory guide and one or two spotters working ahead of you by phone. Golden bamboo lemur and Milne-Edwards's sifaka are the targets and the odds are good before 10:00; leeches after
outings.name: Talatakely, Ranomafana
outings.season: All year. September to December for lemur activity, and it r
outings.fallback: The short Talatakely loop plus the thermal baths in the afternoon.

outings.why: The colder, higher entrance 7 km west on the RN25, with far fewer people, better birds and a real chance at greater bamboo lemur. Steep clay, and the mist can close in for the whole morning.
outings.name: Vohiparara and the high forest
outings.season: All year. Best September to November.

outings.why: A ninety minute walk among granite boulders where about three hundred ring-tailed lemurs live, run entirely by the village association. It is a stop on the long transfer south, not a destination, and it is hot and shadeless after 10:00.
outings.name: Anja and the Ambalavao road
outings.season: All year. September to November for infants on their mothers
outings.fallback: The Antemoro paper works in Ambalavao, twenty minutes.

outings.why: About 350 km of RN7 through Fianarantsoa, Ambalavao and then the long empty Horombe plateau. With the Anja stop it is a full day in the car and you arrive in Ranohira in the dark; this day is the price of the RN7 and nobody enjoys it.
outings.name: Ranomafana to Ranohira
outings.fallback: Sleep at Ambalavao and split it, which costs you a morning in Isalo.

outings.why: Two hours across open sandstone and up a shallow canyon to a cold pool, then the identical ground back with no shade. Guide compulsory, water carried by you, and a 06:30 start is the difference between a good walk and a bad one.
outings.name: The Piscine Naturelle
outings.season: All year. April to October is the comfortable half.
outings.fallback: The Bara tombs and the Interpretation Centre, two hours total.

outings.why: An hour of sand track north, then two narrow canyons holding water and ring-tailed lemurs well into the dry season. The best day in Isalo and the hottest, with the walk out across bare rock in the early afternoon.
outings.name: Canyon des Makis
outings.season: April to November. The track floods in the rains.
outings.fallback: Namaza and the Cascade des Nymphes, shaded and closer.

outings.why: Out by 04:45, forty minutes on the RN8, and the trees go from grey to copper over about twenty-five minutes with zebu carts on the road. Far better than the sunset version, which shares the same hundred metres with every vehicle in Morondav
outings.name: Sunrise at the Allee des Baobabs
outings.season: April to November. The RN8 is frequently impassable January
outings.fallback: The sunset visit the same evening, busier but the same trees.

outings.why: Road transfer to Ambatozavavy, forty-five minutes paddled down the coast in a dugout, then a slow forest walk for black lemurs, panther chameleons and roosting boa, with lunch in the village. The paddle has no shade and the sea can be chopp
outings.name: Lokobe by pirogue
outings.season: All year. April to December is the settled half.
outings.fallback: Mont Passot and the crater lakes in the afternoon.

outings.why: Boat south to a paying marine reserve with turtles on the shallow reef, a beach lunch and a lighthouse climb, usually combined with a stop at Nosy Komba. Every operator lands at the same hour, so the earliest departure is worth paying for.
outings.name: Nosy Tanikely
outings.season: All year. Wind can cancel it June to August.
outings.fallback: Nosy Sakatia for turtles, half the day and calmer water.

destination.name: Madagascar: the RN7, the baobabs and an island
destination.pitch: The wildlife is like nowhere else on earth and the transport is the trip's real subject, so fourteen days buys you about three of these six bases done properly.
destination.caveat: Nothing here is quick: the RN7 runs at about 40 km per hour so Tana to Isalo is two and a half days in a car, the domestic flights to Morondava and Nosy Be are moved or cancelled often enough that you must leave a spare day around each one, a licensed guide is compulsory in every national park and c Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Antananarivo is worth a day and a half for the stairs, the Rova and dinner, and no more than that.
because.food: Honest and narrow. Zebu, rice, romazava and very good freshwater crayfish on the RN7, seafood on the coast, and two or three genuinely good kitchens in Tana.
because.nature: Roughly ninety percent of what lives here lives nowhere else: indri at Andasibe, golden bamboo lemur at Ranomafana, ring-tailed lemurs at Anja and Isalo, Madame Berthe's mouse lemur at Kirindy, and Grandidier's baobabs at Morondava.
because.culture: Highland Merina history at the Rova and Andafiavaratra, Betsileo terraces and the Ambalavao zebu market, Bara tombs in the Isalo cliffs, and famadihana reburials in the highlands in the dry season.
because.adventure: Slot canyons in Isalo, night forest on foot, a dugout paddle to Lokobe and roads that genuinely test a vehicle.
because.relaxation: Only the islands and only after the driving is done. Nosy Be has the sand and the boats; anywhere on the RN7 you will be up at six.
because.exploration: Six landscapes in two weeks, from eastern rainforest to the Horombe plateau to dry western forest, joined by roads that change character every hour.
